title: The chess robot with a person inside
summary: In 1770 a chess-playing machine amazed an empress. A hidden person operated it for the rest of its life.

beats.say: The chess robot that played for an empress had a person inside.
beats.cap: The Turk: a chess robot with a person inside

beats.say: An inventor built it to impress an empress.
beats.cap: Built to impress Empress Maria Theresa

beats.say: Its European tour began in seventeen eighty three.
A later owner took it across America from eighteen twenty six.
All that time, a skilled chess player sat inside the cabinet.
When the cabinet was opened, the operator slid out of view.
beats.cap: The operator slid out of view

beats.say: The operator tracked moves with magnets and moved the arm with levers.
Fire destroyed it in a Philadelphia museum, eighty four years after its debut.
The thinking machine was a person in a box.

claims.note: History.com: the first public performance was in 1770, before Empress Maria Theresa and a group of nobles
History.com: Kempelen's European tour, from 1783 on Joseph II's orders, lasted two years
History.com: Maelzel's U.S. tour began in 1826
Linda Hall Library: destroyed in a fire in Philadelphia on July 5, 1854

facts.claim: Wolfgang von Kempelen built the Turk to impress Empress Maria Theresa; it debuted in 1770
facts.note: History.com: built in 1769 by Kempelen to impress the empress; first public performance in 1770 (Linda Hall Library also dates the unveiling to 1770)

facts.claim: A hidden human chess player operated the Turk from inside the cabinet
facts.note: Linda Hall Library: a 'pseudo-automaton' controlled by a hidden human operator on a sliding chair below the desk

facts.claim: The operator tracked moves with magnetized discs and moved the arm with levers
facts.note: History.com: tracked moves through magnetized discs, moved the arm with levers

facts.claim: Its European tour began in 1783 and Maelzel's U.S. tour in 1826
facts.note: History.com: tour from 1783 on Joseph II's orders; Maelzel's U.S. tour began in 1826

facts.claim: The Turk was destroyed in a fire at a Philadelphia museum in 1854
facts.note: Linda Hall Library: destroyed in a fire at Peale's Museum in Philadelphia, July 5, 1854 (History.com names the Chinese Museum in Philadelphia, same date; the video says only 'a Philadelphia museum')

youtube.hook: The Turk was an 18th-century chess machine that performed for an empress and toured for decades. A hidden chess player operated it from inside the cabinet.
